topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Definition of Database and DBMS
learning_objective: Explain what a database and a DBMS are, including the processes of defining, constructing, manipulating, and sharing databases.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Advantages of DBMS over File Systems
learning_objective: Identify situations where using a database is beneficial over traditional file storage, considering self-describing nature, insulation, multiple views, sharing, and security.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Characteristics and Benefits of Database Systems
learning_objective: Describe key benefits such as data independence, efficient access, integrity enforcement, unauthorized access restriction, backup/recovery, and concurrent access.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Database Design Process Overview
learning_objective: List and explain the six main phases of database development: requirement collection, conceptual design, logical design, schema refinement, physical design, and security design.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Requirement Collection and Analysis
learning_objective: Explain the process of collecting and analyzing user expectations, identifying data to be stored, applications to be built, and operations to be performed, and produce a concise set of user requirements.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Conceptual Database Design using ER Model
learning_objective: Create a conceptual database schema using the Entity-Relationship (ER) model, including entities, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued), and keys.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Binary Relationships and Cardinalities
learning_objective: Draw and interpret binary relationships with cardinality ratios (1:1, 1:N, M:N) based on given scenarios.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Weak Entities
learning_objective: Define weak entities, explain their identifying relationship with the owner entity, and apply the restrictions (one-to-many and total participation).

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Ternary vs. Binary Relationships
learning_objective: Determine when to use a ternary relationship versus binary relationships, especially when a common attribute (e.g., quantity) requires all three entities together.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Specialization and Generalization (EER)
learning_objective: Explain specialization (defining subclasses) and generalization (grouping into superclasses) using ISA relationships, and represent them in an EER diagram.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Overlapping and Covering Constraints
learning_objective: Distinguish between overlapping and disjoint subclasses, and between total (covering) and partial specialization, and apply these constraints in EER diagrams.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Aggregation
learning_objective: Explain aggregation as a way to model a relationship set participating in another relationship, and differentiate it from a ternary relationship.

topic: Introduction to DBMS & Conceptual Database Design
subtopic: Modeling Traps (Fan and Chasm Traps)
learning_objective: Identify and avoid fan traps (ambiguous pathways due to multiple one-to-many relationships from one entity) and chasm traps (missing relationships) in ER models.

subtopic: Logical Database Design and Relational Model Overview
learning_objective: Explain the purpose and process of logical database design, including the selection of a DBMS and the conversion of a conceptual design into a relational schema.

subtopic: Relational Model Components: Relations, Schemas, and Instances
learning_objective: Define the components of the relational model, including relations, relational schemas, and instances (tuples), and represent them as tables.

subtopic: Integrity Constraints: Domain Constraints
learning_objective: Explain domain constraints as a type of integrity constraint that restricts the values in a column to a specified domain or data type.

subtopic: Integrity Constraints: Key Constraints (Candidate and Primary Keys)
learning_objective: Describe key constraints, including candidate keys and primary keys, as minimal sets of attributes that uniquely identify a tuple in a relation.

subtopic: Integrity Constraints: Referential Integrity and Foreign Keys
learning_objective: Explain referential integrity constraints, using foreign keys to ensure consistency between relations, and diagrammatically represent foreign key relationships.

subtopic: Integrity Constraints: Other Constraints (Table Constraints and Assertions)
learning_objective: Identify other integrity constraints such as table constraints (e.g., CHECK constraints) and assertions (e.g., triggers) for enforcing conditions across multiple tables.

subtopic: ER to Relational Mapping: Mapping Entities and Attributes
learning_objective: Map entities and their attributes from an ER diagram to relational tables, defining primary keys for each relation.

subtopic: Mapping Relationships: Binary and N-ary Relationships
learning_objective: Map binary relationships (1:1, 1:N, M:N) and n-ary relationships to relational schemas by creating relationship relations and using foreign keys.

subtopic: Mapping ISA (Specialization/Generalization) Hierarchies: Option 1
learning_objective: Apply Option 1 for mapping ISA relationships by creating a relation for the superclass and separate relations for subclasses, using the superclass primary key as both primary and foreign key, suitable for all constraints (disjoint, overlapping, total, partial).

subtopic: Mapping ISA Hierarchies: Option 2
learning_objective: Apply Option 2 for mapping ISA relationships by creating separate relations for each subclass that include both subclass-specific and superclass attributes, requiring a total specialization (covering constraint).

subtopic: Mapping ISA Hierarchies: Option 3
learning_objective: Apply Option 3 for mapping ISA relationships by creating a single relation with all superclass and subclass attributes plus a 'type' attribute, suitable for disjoint constraints and when subclasses have few attributes.

subtopic: Mapping ISA Hierarchies: Option 4
learning_objective: Apply Option 4 for mapping ISA relationships by creating a single relation with all superclass and subclass attributes plus Boolean attributes for each subclass, allowing overlapping constraints.

subtopic: Mapping Aggregation Relationships
learning_objective: Map aggregation relationships by first mapping the aggregated relationship as an entity set (table), then treating it as an entity set to map higher-level relationships involving the aggregation.

subtopic: Comprehensive EER to Relational Mapping
learning_objective: Convert a complete EER diagram, incorporating entities, relationships, ISA hierarchies, and aggregations, into a set of relational tables following appropriate mapping rules.

subtopic: Pitfalls of Incorrect Attribute Grouping and Need for Schema Refinement
learning_objective: Explain the drawbacks of poorly designed relations, including insertion, deletion, and update anomalies, and data redundancy, using examples.

subtopic: Properties of Good Decomposition: Lossless Join and Dependency Preservation
learning_objective: Define and distinguish between the lossless join property and the dependency preserving property as criteria for evaluating a good decomposition.

subtopic: Definition and Purpose of Functional Dependencies (FDs)
learning_objective: Define a functional dependency and explain its role in identifying redundancies and guiding the normalization process.

subtopic: Computing Attribute Closure and Candidate Keys using Armstrong's Axioms
learning_objective: Compute the closure of an attribute set using Armstrong's axioms (reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity) and identify candidate keys of a relation from a given set of functional dependencies.

subtopic: Key Terminology: Superkey, Candidate Key, Primary Key, Prime and Nonprime Attributes
learning_objective: Define and differentiate between superkey, candidate key, primary key, prime attribute, and nonprime attribute in the context of relational schemas.

subtopic: First Normal Form (1NF) – Atomic Domains
learning_objective: Explain First Normal Form (1NF) as requiring atomic (indivisible) domains for all attributes in a relation.

subtopic: Second Normal Form (2NF) – Full Functional Dependency and Partial Dependency Elimination
learning_objective: Define Second Normal Form (2NF) and eliminate partial dependencies by decomposing a relation, ensuring every nonprime attribute is fully functionally dependent on every candidate key.

subtopic: Third Normal Form (3NF) – Transitive Dependency Elimination
learning_objective: Define Third Normal Form (3NF), identify transitive dependencies involving nonprime attributes, and decompose a relation to eliminate such dependencies.

subtopic: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) – Superkey Requirement for All Nontrivial FDs
learning_objective: Define Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) and apply the BCNF decomposition algorithm to normalize a relation where every nontrivial functional dependency's left side is a superkey.

subtopic: Overview and History of SQL
learning_objective: Explain the origins of SQL (SEQUEL, System R) and its standardization (SQL-86, SQL-92), and describe SQL as a comprehensive database language including DDL, DML, security, transactions, and embedded SQL.

subtopic: SQL Terminology and Relational Model Mapping
learning_objective: Map relational model terms (relation, attribute, tuple) to SQL terms (table, column, row) and use them correctly in SQL statements.

subtopic: Data Definition Language (DDL) – CREATE TABLE and Constraints
learning_objective: Write CREATE TABLE statements to define relations, specifying column data types and constraints such as NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, DEFAULT, and CHECK.

subtopic: DDL – ALTER and DROP Commands
learning_objective: Use ALTER TABLE to add columns or constraints and DROP TABLE to delete tables, modifying the database schema as needed.

subtopic: Data Manipulation Language (DML) – INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE
learning_objective: Write INSERT, DELETE, and UPDATE statements to modify data in tables, including inserting specific columns and using conditions for updates and deletions.

subtopic: Basic SELECT Queries and WHERE Clause
learning_objective: Write basic SELECT statements with attribute lists, FROM clauses, and WHERE conditions to retrieve specific rows and columns from one or more tables.

subtopic: Pattern Matching with LIKE
learning_objective: Use the LIKE operator with wildcard characters % and _ to perform pattern matching on string columns in SQL queries.

subtopic: Checking NULL Values with IS [NOT] NULL
learning_objective: Apply IS NULL and IS NOT NULL operators in WHERE clauses to filter rows based on the presence or absence of null values.

subtopic: Eliminating Duplicates with DISTINCT
learning_objective: Use the DISTINCT keyword to remove duplicate rows from the result set of a SELECT query.

subtopic: Range Conditions with BETWEEN
learning_objective: Write conditions using BETWEEN to check whether a value falls within a specified range, including inclusive boundaries.

subtopic: Sorting Results with ORDER BY
learning_objective: Sort query results using ORDER BY with ASC or DESC options based on one or more columns.

subtopic: Inner Joins
learning_objective: Write SQL queries using INNER JOIN (or comma join with condition) to combine rows from two tables based on a matching condition.

subtopic: Outer Joins (LEFT and RIGHT OUTER JOIN)
learning_objective: Write SQL queries using LEFT OUTER JOIN and RIGHT OUTER JOIN to retrieve all rows from one side of the join, with NULLs for non-matching rows from the other side.

subtopic: Subqueries with IN and EXISTS
learning_objective: Write nested queries using the IN operator for membership tests and the EXISTS operator to check for the existence of rows returned by a subquery.

subtopic: Subqueries with ANY, SOME, and ALL
learning_objective: Write subqueries using ANY, SOME, and ALL operators with comparison operators to compare a value against a list or set of values returned by a subquery.

subtopic: Aggregate Functions (SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX)
learning_objective: Use aggregate functions such as SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, and MAX to compute summary values over a set of rows and return a single result.

subtopic: Grouping with GROUP BY and HAVING
learning_objective: Write SQL queries with GROUP BY to group rows by column values and HAVING to filter groups based on aggregate conditions, following the proper SELECT clause restrictions.

subtopic: Complete SQL Query Structure (Clause Order)
learning_objective: Write complete SQL queries following the correct syntactic order: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY clauses.

subtopic: Views – Definition, Creation, and Querying
learning_objective: Define a view as a virtual table derived from base tables, write CREATE VIEW statements, and query views like regular tables.

subtopic: Views – Update Restrictions and Advantages/Disadvantages
learning_objective: Explain the limitations of updating views (e.g., aggregate functions, joins) and evaluate the trade-offs between security/simplicity and performance/update restrictions.

subtopic: T-SQL Extensions – Variables and Control-of-Flow (IF...ELSE, WHILE)
learning_objective: Write Transact-SQL scripts using local variables (DECLARE, SET), conditional logic (IF...ELSE), and loops (WHILE with BREAK and CONTINUE) to implement server-side logic.

subtopic: User-Defined Functions (Scalar and Table-Valued)
learning_objective: Create SQL functions with input parameters and a return value, and call them from queries or scripts to encapsulate reusable logic.

subtopic: Stored Procedures – Creation and Execution with IN/OUT Parameters
learning_objective: Write stored procedures using CREATE PROCEDURE, define IN and OUT parameters, and execute them with EXEC, retrieving output values for complex business operations.

subtopic: Triggers – Purpose, Types (AFTER, INSTEAD OF), and Virtual Tables
learning_objective: Explain the role of triggers in enforcing business rules and integrity, differentiate between AFTER and INSTEAD OF triggers, and utilize the INSERTED and DELETED virtual tables to respond to DML events.

subtopic: Triggers – Practical Examples for Auditing and Constraint Enforcement
learning_objective: Write triggers to track changes (audit), enforce limits (e.g., maximum withdrawals, number of departments per employee), and maintain cross-table constraints (e.g., salary not exceeding manager's salary).

subtopic: Overview and Purpose of JDBC
learning_objective: Explain the need for a common database access API and define JDBC as an API specification for connecting Java programs to relational databases.

subtopic: JDBC Architecture (JDBC API, DriverManager, Drivers)
learning_objective: Describe the JDBC architecture, including the roles of the JDBC API (application-to-manager), DriverManager (manager-to-driver), and JDBC drivers (driver-to-database).

subtopic: Types of JDBC Drivers (Type 1–4)
learning_objective: Differentiate between the four JDBC driver types (JDBC-ODBC Bridge, Native API, Network Pure Java, and Thin/All-Java driver) in terms of implementation, performance, and deployment.

subtopic: Steps for Using JDBC in a Java Program
learning_objective: List the six essential steps for database programming with JDBC: import packages, load/register the driver, open a connection, execute a query, extract data, and clean up resources.

subtopic: Importing JDBC Packages and Key Interfaces
learning_objective: Import the java.sql package and identify key JDBC interfaces such as Driver, Connection, Statement, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, and ResultSet.

subtopic: Loading and Registering the JDBC Driver
learning_objective: Load and register a JDBC driver dynamically using Class.forName() to initialize the driver class and enable database connectivity.

subtopic: Establishing a Database Connection
learning_objective: Establish a physical database connection using DriverManager.getConnection() with a database URL, username, and password, and close the connection with close().

subtopic: Statement Types: Statement, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement
learning_objective: Choose the appropriate statement type (Statement for static SQL, PreparedStatement for parameterized queries, and CallableStatement for stored procedures) based on the use case.

subtopic: Executing SQL with Statement (execute, executeUpdate, executeQuery)
learning_objective: Execute SQL statements using execute() (general), executeUpdate() (for DML/DDL returning row counts), and executeQuery() (for SELECT returning a ResultSet).

subtopic: Using PreparedStatement with Parameter Markers
learning_objective: Write parameterized SQL queries using PreparedStatement with ? markers, and bind values using setXXX() methods before executing the statement.

subtopic: Using CallableStatement for Stored Procedures
learning_objective: Invoke stored procedures using CallableStatement, including binding input parameters with setXXX(), registering output parameters with registerOutParameter(), and retrieving output values.

subtopic: Processing ResultSet (Cursor Navigation and Data Retrieval)
learning_objective: Traverse a ResultSet using the next() method and retrieve column values using getXXX() methods by either column index or column name.

subtopic: JDBC Exception Handling (SQLException)
learning_objective: Handle JDBC exceptions using SQLException and extract error details with getMessage() and getErrorCode() for debugging vendor-specific errors.

subtopic: Overview of Database Utilities in SQL Server
learning_objective: Identify common database utilities provided by SQL Server, including data transfer tools, job management, backup tools, and maintenance plans, and explain their roles in database administration.

subtopic: Data Transfer Methods and Tools (SSIS, Import/Export Wizard, BCP, BULK INSERT, SELECT INTO)
learning_objective: List and compare different options for transferring data between sources in SQL Server, such as SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS), the Import/Export Wizard, BCP, BULK INSERT, and SELECT INTO.

subtopic: Using the SQL Server Import and Export Wizard (Excel to SQL Server)
learning_objective: Demonstrate the step-by-step process of exporting data from an Excel file to a SQL Server table using the SQL Server Import and Export Wizard, including selecting data sources, mapping columns, and executing the migration.

subtopic: BCP (Bulk Copy Program) Command-Line Utility
learning_objective: Use the BCP command-line utility to export data from a table or query to a data file and to import data, specifying options such as character type, trusted connection, and server name.

subtopic: BULK INSERT Command for Loading Data Files
learning_objective: Write BULK INSERT statements to load data from a flat file into a SQL Server table, defining field and row terminators to correctly parse the input file.

subtopic: SELECT INTO Command for Table-to-Table Copying
learning_objective: Use the SELECT INTO statement to copy data from one table to another, automatically creating the destination table, and explain its use for quick data duplication.

subtopic: Backup and Restore Concepts (Full, Differential, and Transaction Log Backups)
learning_objective: Explain the importance of backing up SQL Server databases and differentiate between full database backups, differential backups, and transaction log backups in terms of their scope and recovery capabilities.

subtopic: Creating and Managing Jobs in SQL Server
learning_objective: Define a SQL Server job as a series of sequential operations, describe how to create jobs with schedules or alerts, and explain the roles of SQL Server Agent and user permissions in job execution.

subtopic: Database Maintenance Plans – Purpose and Typical Tasks
learning_objective: Develop a simple database maintenance plan by identifying critical tasks such as database backups, integrity verification, index maintenance, and cleanup of old backups and history data to ensure adequate performance and availability.

subtopic: Objectives of Database Security (Secrecy, Integrity, Availability)
learning_objective: Explain the three main objectives of database security—secrecy (confidentiality), integrity, and availability—and why protecting data is a critical corporate asset.

subtopic: Security Policies and Access Control Mechanisms (Discretionary vs. Mandatory)
learning_objective: Explain the role of a security policy in specifying user authorizations and distinguish between discretionary access control (privileges) and mandatory access control.

subtopic: SQL Server Security Framework: Authentication, Authorization, Principals, Securables, and Permissions
learning_objective: Describe the SQL Server security framework, differentiating between authentication (verifying identity) and authorization (determining access rights), and define security principals, securables, and permissions.

subtopic: Server-Level Security: Logins and Server Roles
learning_objective: Create Windows and SQL Server authentication logins, assign logins to fixed or user-defined server roles, and grant server-level permissions (e.g., CREATE ANY DATABASE, ALTER ANY LOGIN).

subtopic: Database-Level Security: Users and Database Roles
learning_objective: Create database users mapped to server logins, assign users to fixed database roles (e.g., db_owner, db_ddladmin, db_securityadmin) and user-defined database roles to manage database-level access.

subtopic: Managing Permissions with GRANT, DENY, and REVOKE
learning_objective: Manage database permissions by applying GRANT, DENY, and REVOKE statements on securables to principals, covering permissions such as SELECT, INSERT, CREATE TABLE, REFERENCES, and EXECUTE.

subtopic: Using Views as an Access Control Mechanism
learning_objective: Explain how views can be used as a security tool to restrict user access to specific data and hide underlying table structures, requiring appropriate privileges on the underlying tables.
